message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $306 and three unmortgaged streets. p1 has $1014 and a complete light-blue set plus utilities. p2 has $166 on Pacific.

p2 has a green monopoly with three houses on Pacific and NC, two on Pennsylvania. p3 has a dark-blue set built up to two houses on Park Place and three on Boardwalk. The bank holds Oriental, Kentucky, and Atlantic unowned. I just passed GO and landed on Baltic, which was auctioned for $80.

The brown set is split between p1 and p2, so neither has a brown monopoly. p1 holds Vermont and Connecticut but not Oriental, leaving the light-blue set incomplete. The orange set is complete with St James, Tennessee, and New York.

I block the orange and pink monopolies. The red and yellow sets are split. The green set is dangerous. The dark-blue set is extremely dangerous with Boardwalk at three houses and Park Place at two.

I will keep all four blockers. Unmortgaging Marvin Gardens costs $154, leaving only $152 cash, so I will not do it. The yellow block is too expensive to restore right now.

I am calculating the next roll outcomes from Baltic. Oriental is unowned at $100 and would block p1's light-blue set if I buy it. Vermont and Connecticut are both owned by p1 for base rent. The Electric Company is owned by p1, so landing there would cost 10× dice.

I will not trade. Selling any blocker would let a richer opponent build and destroy me. p2 has the green monopoly but only $166 cash, so they are less threatening than p3.

I will not mortgage any properties. My cash is sufficient to buy Oriental for $100 and cover small rent payments. Mortgaging would only reduce my blocking rent income, and the properties would still block monopolies while mortgaged.

I will end the turn. I considered trading with p2 or p3, but p3 cannot afford to unmortgage and build the pink set immediately.
